impl.summary: Blockout to film is built and pushed (8 commits on claude/fuobe-parity-4 at 6bcb1e63). You can upload a grey-box render from any 3D app, build one in the browser, or use the 3D scene's fly path as a blockout. Beats come from markers. Reference stills each get a role. The prompt is compiled in the Horror-scene workflow's sections and can be edited. Cloud: Seedance 2.5 reference mode, or MiniMax H3 Max 3D to video under its own name; a blockout too long for one call is cut into shots at the markers, each shot gets the previous shot's last frame as a still, and the shots are joined. Open engine: a new Wan 2.2 Fun VACE graph driven by the blockout's own depth, starting from a first frame drawn from the stills, in 81-frame windows that are chained and joined. Also placed in the Cinema composer, the 3D scene viewer, a Canvas template, Assist/MCP and the GPU board.
built: src/lib/blockout.ts (pure): the builder's scene (box, wall, floor, doorway, stairs, door on a hinge, mannequin, mesh), primitive keys, camera keys (eased moves, lens, deterministic handheld shake), timing markers, the corridor-and-door example (Fuobe's own), normalizeScene, beatsFrom / normalizeBeats, reference roles with role sentences, compileBlockoutPrompt (seedance: @Video1/@Image1… in Subject/Action 'a–b s — beat: …'/Camera/Style/Constraints/Audio/No; h3: no tags, capped at 2000 chars; open: a short Wan prompt), blockoutFramePrompt, beatsIn, splitShots (cut at markers within each model's limit), depthWindows (81 frames at 16 fps, each window starting on the previous one's last frame, 4n+1 frames).

Catalog: Cinema action 'blockout' (CinemaGenerateInput.blockout, planBlockout, blockoutPrompt, blockoutTake, BLOCKOUT_MODELS / BLOCKOUT_SHOTS, feature cinema-blockout, take info), the server schema (BlockoutSchema: /api/files refs only, at most 60 s), recordTakes keeps the blockout facts.

New hosted helper minimax-h3-max-3d (fal minimax/h3-max/3d-to-video, op v2v). Its research record was added to paid-model-apis-4.json from fal's OpenAPI read today, and generated by scripts/gen-cloud-models.py. Pricing gained perRequest and minSeconds ($0.50 processing fee per request, at least 5 s billed per shot).

New ComfyUI graph video-blockout-wan22-fun-vace (hand-built; the restyle graph without Depth Anything 3, with the depth video as the control and silent output) and the open model oss-wan22-vace-blockout (v2v + ref2v). Validated against the CPU ComfyUI with --shared. Manifest header and object_info.subset.json were restored to their earlier values after the build/validate wrote the local ComfyUI 0.41's details over them, and requirements.json was rebuilt. No new node packs or model files.

Browser: blockout-engine.ts (three.js: orbit view with a move/turn gizmo, shot-camera view letterboxed to the frame, walking mannequin, GLB meshes from the Library shown in grey, grey render and depth render with near = bright), blockout-builder.tsx (Build/Piece/Camera/Beats tabs, timeline with play, scrub, camera-key and marker ticks), blockout-panel.tsx (upload or build, optional depth pass, beats with words, stills from upload/Elements/Soul Cast/Soul Location/Library with a role each, style/sounds/No/rules, cloud model choice, quality, sound toggle, editable compiled prompt, notes, price, 'Film it', and a 'Sound for video' next step for silent results). A Blockout chip in the composer, 'Use as blockout' in the 3D scene viewer (renders the path at 24 fps), and /cinema/<id>?blockout=1 opens the panel.

src/lib/mp4.ts: an MP4 (H.264) writer, because Seedance takes reference clips as MP4/MOV only. src/components/cinema/video-encode.ts: the fly path's VP8/WebM encoders moved here unchanged, plus encodeMp4 / encodeFrames.

Canvas: a 'Blockout → film' template that builds per engine (cloud: Seedance 2.5 ref2v with the blockout in a new Clips port that ref2v models taking clips now show, three stills and the compiled beats; open: Qwen first frame, then the depth graph for one window). The Box icon is registered.
Assist/MCP: a blockout_film tool that plans with Cinema's planBlockout and runs as a Library pipeline; it is named in Assist's system prompt.
GPU pre-flight board: a 'Blockout to film' row (href /cinema?blockout=1) on video-blockout-wan22-fun-vace, qwen-image-edit-2511-multi, video-segment-resample, frame-extract, video-concat-encoded.
Research: new-models-10.json marks H3 Max 3D to video as built (schema re-read) and records SolarRenderer as re-read at its primary sources.
impl.tests: FULL Vitest (FUOBE_ACCOUNT_DISK_FREE_GB=1, --maxWorkers=2): 288 files, 4596 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed. tsc clean; eslint 0 errors (1 warning, already in scripts/comfy/library.spec.mjs). New tests: tests/blockout.test.ts (32 tests: scene maths, shake, lens, normalizeScene, beats, prompt sections and @ tags, H3 2000-character cap, roles, shot splitting, depth windows, cloud plans for one shot / many shots / H3, open plans with and without depth, pricing incl. the H3 fee and minimum, H3 and Seedance payloads, binding of the new graph, the Cinema API in demo, the schema refusing bad input, the Canvas template, the GPU row, Assist/MCP plan and run), tests/mp4.test.ts (box layout, plus ffmpeg decoding the writer's output frame for frame), a Board row in public-signup-tools, a blockout_film sample in assist-context; the template-covers tile count went from 228 to 229. ComfyUI: video-blockout-wan22-fun-vace validated on the live CPU ComfyUI (queued and removed, never run: no weights). Browser: tests/e2e/cinema-blockout.mjs passed in demo mode at 1440 light (built the example, rendered it in the browser to 192 H.264 frames at 1280x720 and a 128-frame 832x464 depth video, both checked with ffprobe; still + role; compiled prompt; filmed on Seedance), 1440 dark open engine (uploaded MP4, hand-made beats, Free, open steps queued), and 390 light/dark (panel and builder, no sideways scroll). Dev server stopped and .next deleted.
left: Not verified on a GPU or with a fal key: the Seedance 2.5 and H3 Max 3D cloud runs and the Wan 2.2 Fun VACE blockout windows only ran in demo mode, and the new graph was validated, not run. On the real GPU run, check the near = bright depth convention against Fun VACE's control.

SolarRenderer (the H3 grey-box route on the open engine) is recorded, not built. It needs smthemex/ComfyUI-SolarRenderer (Apache-2.0, git clone only, not in the Manager) plus the MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA base and its LoRAs (MiniMax H3 Community License, which excludes the EU, UK, Korea and the US). Next step: install it on a GPU box, pin it in packs.json and model-pins.json, and A/B it against the VACE windows.

Long cloud blockouts carry continuity by handing the previous shot's last frame to the next shot as an extra still (extract-frame), then join-clips. Seedance's own extend op was not used: it can't take the blockout segment beside the clip it extends.
On the open engine each window starts on the previous window's last frame, so the joined film repeats one frame (1/16 s) at each 5 s seam. The open engine renders at most 12 windows (about 60 s).
The mannequin is Fuobe's own capsule figure in the browser. The Rig & animate rigged figure was not reused: it is made server-side, not a browser rig.
GLB files can't be uploaded (the upload route doesn't take model/*), so 'Your 3D model' lists Library 3D models (Image to 3D outputs).
Browsers without WebCodecs H.264 fall back to WebM, and the panel warns that the cloud may refuse it. The test's Chromium did encode H.264.
The GPU board row links to /cinema?blockout=1. The projects list ignores the query (only /cinema/<id>?blockout=1 opens the panel). A Suspense-wrapped search-param read on /cinema would fix it.

Seen, not caused here: a hydration mismatch in the app sidebar (ViewerRowPlaceholder) at desktop width with the engine set to open, on /cinema/<id> with or without the blockout query. The new e2e ignores 'Hydration failed'. The existing tests/e2e/cinema-path.mjs open-engine step will probably trip on it.
The owner's Horror_Scene_SD2.5.json was not available; I worked from the brief. /home/user/ext/blockout is missing.

findings.title: An edited prompt for H3 Max 3D goes to fal uncapped, but fal allows at most 2000 characters
findings.where: src/lib/catalog/cinema.ts planBlockout (const prompt = !many && input.prompt.trim() ? input.prompt.trim() : compiled); src/components/cinema/blockout-panel.tsx Textarea (slice 0..60_000); src/server/assist/studio-tools.ts BlockoutInput.prompt max(60_000)
findings.detail: Only the compiled prompt is capped (compileBlockoutPrompt caps h3 at H3_INTENT_MAX). Once the user edits the prompt in the composer, or Assist/MCP passes `prompt`, a single-shot H3 film sends it as written. fal's schema for minimax/h3-max/3d-to-video, re-read today, says prompt maxLength is 2000 and additionalProperties is false, so a longer prompt fails with 422 after the run has been accepted. No generic prompt-length guard exists in the catalog or payload layer.
findings.verified: Ran planCinema with tsx (cloud, minimax-h3-max-3d, 10 s, prompt 'x'×5000): shot0.request.prompt.length = 5000. fal OpenAPI: prompt maxLength 2000.
findings.fix: Cap or refuse with a clear message when the model is H3 (cap(prompt, H3_INTENT_MAX) or a blocker), and limit the textarea to 2000 for H3.

findings.title: Seedance 2.5 blockout prices ignore fal's billing for the input video and the resolution
findings.where: src/lib/catalog/cloud-models.generated.ts seedance-2-5 pricing {unit: second, usd: 0.473} (from scripts/gen-cloud-models.py); priced by planBlockout / estimateCost
findings.detail: fal's Seedance 2.5 reference-to-video page bills by tokens on input video seconds plus output seconds, times 0.6 when video references are present: tokens = h × w × (input + output) × 24 / 1024, at $0.0214 per 1K tokens (480p/720p) and $0.0234 (1080p). Every Blockout call sends a reference clip, yet the estimate is 0.473 × output seconds whatever the resolution. For a 10 s blockout the plan says $4.73 at 480p, 720p and 1080p alike. By fal's formula that is about $5.5 at 720p (15% low), about $13.6 at 1080p (2.9× low) and about $2.5 at 480p (too high). The catalog data was already wrong on the base, but this package depends on it, and the brief asks for the film to be 'priced before running'. Pricing.clipInput (used by Kling 4.0) already models input-plus-output billing. tests/blockout.test.ts asserts the wrong rule (cost ≥ 40 × 0.473).
findings.verified: tsx probe: seedance-2-5, 10 s, at 480p / 720p / 1080p, all cost 4.73. Fetched fal.ai/models/bytedance/seedance-2.5/reference-to-video: 'input video duration is billed alongside output', ×0.6 with video references, the token formula and rates.
findings.fix: Give seedance-2-5 a byResolution / clipInput pricing (or a token formula) in gen-cloud-models.py, with a test against fal's formula.

findings.title: H3 shots can be cut down to 2 s, but each one is billed at least 5 s plus a $0.50 fee
findings.detail: splitShots leaves at least `min` seconds for the last shot. With min 2, a 16 s H3 blockout becomes a 14 s shot and a 2 s shot. fal bills the 2 s shot as 5 s, plus another $0.50 fee. The plan prices this correctly at $2.52, but splitting 11 + 5 would give the same number of calls for about $2.28 and less waste. Using min 5 (H3's billing floor) avoids paying for seconds that are thrown away.
findings.verified: tsx probe: 16 s H3 gives shot durations 14 and 2, cost 2.523.

findings.title: The H3 price leaves out two of fal's charges: auto-generated references, and the 5 s minimum per cut inside an uploaded blockout
findings.detail: fal's page: references are generated automatically when none are supplied (max_generated_reference_images defaults to 2), at $0.10 per image (the page also says $0.02–0.04). Fuobe sends no references when the user adds no stills, and sends no max_generated_reference_images, so the first shot can cost up to $0.20 more than shown. fal also bills 'a minimum of 5 billed seconds per shot', where a shot is a cut inside the source video (up to 32). An uploaded Blender blockout with cuts is billed more than Fuobe's one-call minimum. The research record mentions both charges; the price and the UI note do not.
findings.verified: fal model page and OpenAPI, read today; estimateCost has no such term.

findings.title: GPU board row: its link doesn't open Blockout, and it leaves out the graph used for uploads without a depth pass
findings.detail: (1) href '/cinema?blockout=1' goes to the projects list, which ignores the query; only /cinema/<id>?blockout=1 opens the panel (workspace.tsx). The implementer also noted this. (2) The row's steps are BLOCKOUT_MODELS.open, oss-qwen-edit, oss-segment, oss-extract-frame and oss-join-encoded. An uploaded grey box without a depth pass is the common Blender case, and it runs BLOCKOUT_MODELS.openNoDepth (video-restyle-wan22-fun-vace). That graph needs DA3 nodes and geometry_estimation/depth_anything_3_mono_large.safetensors (requirements.json). The board can therefore say Ready while that path is missing its model file.
findings.verified: Read src/app/(studio)/cinema/page.tsx (no query handling), workspace.tsx:219-221, and requirements.json for video-restyle-wan22-fun-vace.

findings.title: An uploaded depth pass gets no guidance on its convention (near = bright), and a Blender mist pass is the opposite
findings.where: src/components/cinema/blockout-panel.tsx 'Add a depth pass'; src/lib/catalog/cinema.ts BlockoutRun.depth doc ('Blender's mist / Z pass works too')
findings.detail: The graph feeds the depth video to VACE as it is. Blender's mist pass is near = dark by default, and a raw Z pass is not normalised. The panel says nothing about this, so a user who follows the code comment gets an inverted control video with no warning. Assist's schema states near = bright; the UI does not.
findings.verified: Code reading; grep found no 'near = bright' or invert option in the panel.

findings.title: The blockout's length is the client's word; if an upload's duration can't be read, the panel silently assumes 8 s
findings.where: blockout-panel.tsx uploadVideo (secs fallback 8); src/server/cinema-schemas.ts BlockoutSchema.seconds (not compared with the stored file)
findings.detail: When mediaDuration fails (for example a MOV the browser can't decode), seconds becomes 8. The plan then sends the whole clip as @Video1 with duration 8 and no split, even if the clip is 40 s, and fal refuses clips over 30.2 s. The trims and windows are also timed to the wrong length. The server already has the upload's header (storedMedia, which Assist's blockout_film reads through videoLength) but doesn't use it for Cinema.

findings.title: WebM blockouts reach Seedance with no warning on two paths
findings.detail: Seedance's video_urls take MP4/MOV only. The builder warns when it falls back to WebM, but 'Use as blockout' in the 3D scene viewer (encodeFrames can fall back to VP8 or MediaRecorder WebM) and a WebM upload do not. A single-shot Seedance film sends the WebM unchanged, so the cloud refuses it after the run starts. Multi-shot films pass through trim-video first.
findings.verified: Code reading; fal schema: 'Formats: MP4, MOV'.

findings.title: Keyboard users can't frame camera keys or move pieces that have keys
findings.detail: Camera keys copy the orbit view. OrbitControls never calls listenToKeyEvents, and there are no numeric fields for camera position or target. Pieces with keys lose their Position and Turn fields (`!prim.keys?.length`), so adding a key needs the pointer gizmo. Static pieces, lens, shake, markers and the playhead do work from the keyboard. The brief asks for keyboard users to be covered.
findings.verified: grep: no listenToKeyEvents or keydown handling in either file.

findings.title: The new e2e ignores every 'Hydration failed' error
findings.detail: The sidebar mismatch is real and pre-existing (see checks), but a blanket filter would also hide hydration errors introduced by the Blockout panel or builder. A filter that matches only the known ViewerRowPlaceholder diff would be safer.
findings.verified: Read the test; reproduced the pre-existing error separately.

findings.title: For many-shot Seedance films, the composer's prompt preview numbers the stills differently from what each shot sends
findings.detail: The preview compiles with up to 4 stills (@Image4 = the 4th still). A many-shot film sends 3 stills plus the hand-over frame as @Image4 in each shot. Only the preview is affected: an edited prompt is not used for many-shot films, and the notes say so.

findings.title: mp4.ts is correct; memory use is fine but not minimal
findings.detail: Checked box by box against ISO BMFF: mvhd/tkhd/mdhd/hdlr/vmhd/dref/avc1 VisualSampleEntry/avcC/stts/stss/stsc/stsz/stco are all well formed; stco = ftyp + moov + 8; 90 kHz timescale. Frames are encoded as they are drawn (one reused ImageData; VideoFrame copies it), so raw frames are never held in memory. At the end the encoded data is copied about 3 times (box() concat of mdat, the box wrapper, the final concat), and once more into the Blob: about 4× the file size at peak, roughly 240 MB for 60 s at 8 Mbps. Acceptable. Handing the Blob [ftyp, moov, mdat header, ...frames] as BlobParts would avoid the copies. The writer assumes no B-frames: true for baseline (tried first) and for Chromium's encoders; a check that timestamps increase would make that safe.

review.verdict: Merge after fixes. The package is solid: the MP4 writer is correct and verified by a real decoder in the browser, the shot and window maths and the new graph's bindings check out against the live ComfyUI, the H3 schema, fee and 5 s minimum match fal, and no sign-up rule is broken. Fix the two medium issues before relying on real cloud runs: cap or refuse an H3 prompt edited past 2000 characters (fal returns 422), and correct Seedance 2.5's reference-to-video price (input plus output seconds, per resolution), so the price shown before running is right. The low items (H3 shot minimum, unpriced H3 extras, the board row's link and missing restyle graph, depth-pass guidance, the trusted length, WebM warnings, keyboard framing, the e2e's hydration filter) can follow. The sidebar hydration error is on the base too and is not caused by this branch.

applied: Medium, H3 prompt: planBlockout refuses an edited one-shot prompt over 2000 characters for MiniMax H3 Max 3D to video with a clear blocker (BLOCKOUT_SHOTS[..].prompt = H3_INTENT_MAX), so neither the composer nor Assist/MCP can send it. The composer's prompt box is limited to 2000 for H3 (maxLength plus slice) and shows an 'n / 2000 characters' count; Assist's prompt field says so. Tests: 2000 passes, 5000 refused, Seedance and many-shot H3 not affected; e2e checks maxlength=2000.

Medium, Seedance 2.5 price: I re-read fal's reference-to-video page and OpenAPI (2026-11-01). Tokens = h×w×(input + output seconds)×24/1024 at $0.0214 per 1K (480p/720p) or $0.0234 (1080p), ×0.6 with video references. fal's sidebar $0.473/s divides by 1000 where the formula says 1024. In gen-cloud-models.py, seedance-2-5 now has byResolution {480p 0.21494, 720p 0.46224, 1080p 1.13724} and clipInput {480p 0.12897, 720p 0.27734, 1080p 0.68234, plain: true}. Pricing.clipInput.plain bills input + output with no twice-output floor; a clip not yet read is taken as long as the output; the server reprices from the header (billsClips) as it already did for Kling. planBlockout sends clipSeconds = the shot's length (the blockout or its cut). A note says the blockout's seconds are billed with the film's. The composer's 'at least twice' wording only shows when the floor applies. Tests reproduce fal's own worked examples ($4.62, $4.99, $11.09) and the per-resolution formula. The wrong '≥ 40 × 0.473' assertion is replaced by the formula.
Low, H3 shot minimum: BLOCKOUT_SHOTS H3 min is now 5, so 16 s is cut 11 + 5 instead of 14 + 2 (tested).

Low, H3 extra charges: new Pricing.generatedRefs {usd 0.10, count 2} and GenParams.drawnRefs, set by planGeneration when a run sends no images and chains none. A run with no stills prices the up to 2 references fal draws (max_generated_reference_images has a minimum of 1 and is ignored when stills are given, so 0 can't be sent). Notes: the drawn references and their price, and that every camera cut inside an uploaded render bills at least 5 s. Tests for one shot, multi-shot (only the first shot draws) and estimateCost.

Low, GPU board row: the row now also needs BLOCKOUT_MODELS.openNoDepth (video-restyle-wan22-fun-vace, DA3). /cinema?blockout=1 now works: a Suspense-wrapped useSearchParams child in the projects list shows 'Blockout to film: pick the project to film it in', and project cards and a new project carry ?blockout=1, which opens the panel (e2e step). Test updated.

Low, depth convention: the panel says 'near is bright, far is dark' under the depth pass. A 'Near is dark (Blender's mist pass): invert it' switch sets BlockoutRun.depthInvert. The open plan sends params.extra.invertDepth to every window. The graph video-blockout-wan22-fun-vace gained PrimitiveBoolean → ComfySwitchNode(on_false raw, on_true ImageInvert) before the control batch, bound as invertDepth (added to BINDING_KEYS, with a validator sample of true). It was rebuilt and validated on the live CPU ComfyUI with --shared: inverted branch ✓; nothing queued ran. The manifest header and object_info.subset.json were kept at the base's values, and requirements.json was rebuilt. The BlockoutRun mist/Z comment is corrected. Assist takes depth_invert. Tests: plan extra, graph wiring, binding false/true; e2e uploads a mist pass, ticks invert, checks invertDepth on the run.

Low, trusted length: new blockoutFromFile (src/server/cinema-generate.ts) reads the stored file's header with storedMedia (allContainers, header only, tenant-safe). Cinema's generate (plan and take) and Assist's blockout_film use the header's length (capped at 60 s) over the browser's, and mark WebM. The builder can be driven from the keyboard: typed camera keys, typed poses for moving pieces, arrow keys in the 3D view.
